extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, and registered patent practitioners (including USPTO examiners and staff)
extracted.subtask_short: maintenance fees and PCT filing rules
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedural standards for paying U.S. patent maintenance fees (including surcharges, fee addresses, payment methods, petitions for refusal/delayed payment) and for filing/processing international (PCT) applications (office roles, applicant eligibility, required contents, fee timing and late-payment rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fee surcharge periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Surcharge set forth in § 1.20(h) applies during the respective grace periods after: (1) 3 years and 6 months and through the day of the 4th anniversary of the grant for the first maintenance fee; (2) 7 years and 6 months and through the day of the 8th anniversary of the grant for the second maintenance fee; and (3) 11 years and 6 months and through the day of the 12th anniversary of the grant for the third maintenance fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the prescribed surcharge/grace windows; see § 1.20(h) for surcharge amounts. If the maintenance fee and any applicable surcharge is not paid within these periods, the patent will expire as of the end of the relevant grace period (§ 1.362(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekend/holiday payment extension rule
rubrics_metrics.description: If the last day for paying a maintenance fee without surcharge or with surcharge falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or a federal holiday within the District of Columbia, the maintenance fee and any necessary surcharge may be paid on the next succeeding day which is not a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides the standard extension similar to other filing-deadline rules; applicable to the last day for paying under paragraphs (d), (e), or (f) of § 1.362.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent expiration for failure to pay maintenance fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the maintenance fee and any applicable surcharge is paid within the time periods set forth in paragraphs (d), (e) or (f) of § 1.362, the patent will expire as of the end of the grace period set forth in paragraph (e) of § 1.362. A patent which expires for the failure to pay the maintenance fee will expire at the end of the same date (anniversary date) the patent was granted in the 4th, 8th, or 12th year after grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expiration occurs automatically at end of the relevant grace period; petition procedures (e.g., § 1.378) are available only in limited circumstances to revive by showing unintentional delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue maintenance-period counting
rubrics_metrics.description: The periods specified in §§ 1.362(d) and (e) with respect to a reissue application, including a continuing reissue application thereof, are counted from the date of grant of the original non-reissue application on which the reissued patent is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When paying maintenance fees for reissue patents, use the original patent's grant date to determine the applicable maintenance window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee address for maintenance fee purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices, receipts, refunds, and other communications relating to payment or refund of maintenance fees will be directed to the correspondence address used during prosecution (§ 1.33(a)) unless: (1) a fee address for purposes of payment of maintenance fees is set when submitting the issue fee; (2) a change in the correspondence address for all purposes is filed after payment of the issue fee; or (3) a fee address or a change in the 'fee address' is filed for purposes of receiving notices/receipts after payment of the issue fee, in which instance the latest such address will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An assignment does not change correspondence/fee address for maintenance purposes. A fee address must be an address associated with a Customer Number (§ 1.363(b)-(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may pay maintenance fees and signature/authorization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee may pay maintenance fees and any necessary surcharges, or any person or organization may pay maintenance fees and any necessary surcharges on behalf of a patentee. A maintenance fee transmittal letter may be signed by a juristic applicant or patent owner. A patentee need not file authorization to enable any person or organization to pay maintenance fees and any necessary surcharges on behalf of the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments may be submitted in the manner set forth in § 1.23 or by authorization to charge a deposit account under § 1.25. Any authorization to charge a deposit account must authorize the immediate charging of the maintenance fee and any necessary surcharge. Payment procedures in § 1.8 or § 1.10 may also be utilized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount and method of payment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A maintenance fee and any necessary surcharge submitted for a patent must be submitted in the amount due on the date the maintenance fee and any necessary surcharge are paid. Payment of less than the required amount, payment in a manner other than that set forth in § 1.23, or filing an authorization to charge a deposit account having insufficient funds will not constitute payment of a maintenance fee or surcharge on a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure full amount and correct payment method; otherwise payment will not be accepted (except insofar as delayed payment accepted by Director via petition under § 1.378).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification required with maintenance-fee payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of the patents for which maintenance fees are being paid must include the patent number, and the application number of the United States application for the patent on which the maintenance fee is being paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If payment includes only the patent number (no application number), the Office may apply the payment to the patent identified or return the payment. Payments should identify whether it is the 3½-, 7½-, or 11½-year fee, whether small-entity status is being changed or claimed, amount of fee and surcharge, and any assigned customer number. For reissue patents, identify the reissue patent number and reissue application number and should include the original patent number (§ 1.366(c)-(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate submission and ordering of maintenance-fee payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fee payments and surcharge payments relating thereto must be submitted separate from any other payments for fees or charges. If maintenance fee and surcharge payments for more than one patent are submitted together, they should be submitted on as few sheets as possible with the patent numbers listed in increasing patent number order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the payment submitted is insufficient to cover the maintenance fees and surcharges for all listed patents, the payment will be applied in the order the patents are listed, beginning at the top of the listing (§ 1.366(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in small entity status notification timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification of any change in status resulting in loss of entitlement to small entity status must be filed in a patent prior to paying, or at the time of paying, the earliest maintenance fee due after the date on which status as a small entity is no longer appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.27(g) for rules on small entity status; failure to timely notify may affect fee amounts and entitlements (§ 1.366(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund policy for maintenance fees and surcharges
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees and surcharges relating thereto will not be refunded except in accordance with §§ 1.26 and 1.28(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refunds are tightly restricted to the statutory/regulatory channels specified in referenced sections (§ 1.366(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to review refusal to accept and record payment filed prior to expiration (§ 1.377)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any patentee dissatisfied with the refusal of the PTO to accept and record a maintenance fee filed prior to expiration may petition the Director to accept and record the maintenance fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must be filed within two months of the action complained of (or other time set in the action) and be accompanied by the fee in § 1.17(g). The petition may request refund of the petition fee if PTO error caused the refusal. The petition must comply with § 1.181(b) and be signed by a registered attorney/agent, the patentee, assignee, or other party in interest (§ 1.377(b)-(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of delayed payment of maintenance fee in expired patent (§ 1.378)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may accept the payment of any maintenance fee due on a patent after expiration if, upon petition, the delay in payment is shown to the satisfaction of the Director to have been unintentional. If accepted, the patent shall be considered as not having expired, but will be subject to the conditions set forth in 35 U.S.C. 41(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance is discretionary and conditioned on proof of unintentional delay; statutory limitations under 35 U.S.C. 41(c)(2) apply (§ 1.378(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and fees for petition to accept unintentionally delayed payment (§ 1.378(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any petition to accept an unintentionally delayed payment of a maintenance fee must include: (1) the required maintenance fee set forth in § 1.20(e) through (g); (2) the petition fee as set forth in § 1.17(m); and (3) a statement that the delay in payment of the maintenance fee was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional. The petition must be signed in compliance with § 1.33(b). Reconsideration of a refusal may be obtained by filing a petition for reconsideration within two months (or other time set) (§ 1.378(b)-(e)). If delayed payment not accepted, the maintenance fee will be refunded following final decision or after time for reconsideration expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States Receiving Office identification and core functions (RO/US)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent and Trademark Office, when acting as a Receiving Office, will be identified by the full title 'United States Receiving Office' or by the abbreviation 'RO/US.' Major functions include: according international filing dates to international applications meeting PCT Art. 11(1) and PCT Rule 20; assuring that international applications meet format/content standards (PCT Art. 14(1), PCT Rule 9, 26, 29.1, 37, 38, 91, and portions of PCT Rules 3-11); collecting/transmitting fees due for processing international applications (PCT Rule 14, 15, 16); transmitting record and search copies to the International Bureau and International Searching Authority (PCT Rules 22 and 23); and determining compliance with applicable requirements of part 5 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RO/US may also review and transmit applications to the IB for processing unless prescriptions concerning national security prevent transmission (PCT Rule 19.4); see § 1.412 and related paragraphs for specific transmission conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States International Searching Authority functions (ISA/US)
rubrics_metrics.description: When acting as an International Searching Authority, the PTO will be identified as 'United States International Searching Authority' or 'ISA/US.' Major ISA functions include: approving or establishing the title and abstract; considering unity of invention; conducting international and international-type searches and preparing search reports (PCT Art. 15, 17, 18; PCT Rules 25, 33-45, 47); issuing declarations that no international search report will be established (PCT Art. 17(2)(a)); and preparing written opinions of the International Searching Authority in accordance with PCT Rule 43 bis (when necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISA's search and written opinion are foundational to international prosecution and may affect national-stage processing (§ 1.413 and related paragraphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: United States International Preliminary Examining Authority functions (IPEA/US)
rubrics_metrics.description: When acting as an International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA/US), major functions include: receiving and checking for defects in the Demand; forwarding Demands under PCT Rule 59.3; collecting handling and preliminary examination fees; informing applicant of receipt of the Demand; considering unity of invention; providing an international preliminary examination report which is a non-binding opinion on whether the claimed invention appears novel, to involve an inventive step (nonobvious), and to be industrially applicable; and transmitting the international preliminary examination report to applicant and the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The international preliminary examination report is non-binding but addresses patentability criteria (novelty, inventive_step/nonobviousness, industrial_applicability) and is transmitted to applicant and IB (§ 1.416 and related paragraphs).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau (IB) functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau (WIPO) major functions include publishing international applications and the International Gazette; transmitting copies of international applications to Designated Offices; storing and maintaining record copies; and transmitting information to authorities pertinent to processing specific international applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB handles publication and dissemination functions critical to the international stage; see § 1.415 for details and relation to PCT Art. 2(xix) and 35 U.S.C. 351(h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an international application in RO/US (applicant eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only residents or nationals of the United States of America may file international applications in the United States Receiving Office. For designation of the United States, an international application will be accepted by the PTO for the national stage only if the applicant is the inventor or as provided in §§ 1.422 or 1.424. Joint inventors must jointly apply for an international application. A registered attorney or agent may sign the Request and file for the applicant; separate power of attorney from each applicant may be required. Indications of different applicants for different Designated Offices must be shown on the Request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an international application does not include an applicant indicated as a US resident/national and at least one applicant has indicated residence/nationality in a PCT Contracting State or no residence indicated, the applicant will be notified and the application may be forwarded to the IB acting as a Receiving Office if equivalent fees are included (§ 1.421). Changes and withdrawals of indications, priority claims, the Demand, or elections must follow PCT Rule 90bis and typically must be signed by all applicants (§ 1.421 and related notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal representative, assignee, or proprietary-interest applicant rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inventor is deceased or under legal incapacity, the legal representative of the inventor may be an applicant in an international application which designates the United States. A person to whom the inventor has assigned or is under an obligation to assign the invention, or who otherwise shows sufficient proprietary interest, may be an applicant in an international application which designates the United States (proof of facts and showing that action is appropriate to preserve rights may be required). Documentary proof is not required/considered at the international stage but will be required in the national stage per § 1.46.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These applicant substitutions/assignee rules are subject to specific effective-date caveats (post-/pre-AIA distinctions) and to national-stage documentary requirements (§§ 1.422, 1.422(pre-AIA), 1.424).

rubrics_metrics.name: International application required contents for receiving an international filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application shall contain a Request, a description, one or more claims, an abstract, and one or more drawings (where required). An international filing date will be accorded by the United States Receiving Office provided that: (1) at least one applicant is a US resident or national and the papers show that; (2) the international application is in the English language; and (3) the international application contains at least the following elements: (i) an indication that it is intended as an international application (PCT Rule 4.2); (ii) the designation of at least one Contracting State; (iii) the name of the applicant; (iv) a part which on its face appears to be a description; and (v) a part which on its face appears to be a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the minimum filing-date formalities under PCT Art. 11(1) and related provisions; additional documentary/fee steps follow (§ 1.431(b)-(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment timing and late-payment rules for international filing/transmittal/search fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment of the international filing fee (PCT Rule 15.2) and the transmittal and search fees (§ 1.445) may be made in full at the time the international application papers are deposited or within one month thereafter. The international filing, transmittal, and search fee payable is the fee in effect on the receipt date of the international application. If such fees are not paid within one month from the date of receipt and prior to sending of a notice of deficiency (which imposes a late payment fee), applicant will be notified and given a one-month non-extendable time limit to pay the deficient fees plus the late payment fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the payment needed to cover the transmittal, filing, search, and late payment fee is not timely made in accordance with PCT Rule 16bis.1(e), the Receiving Office will declare the international application withdrawn under PCT Article 14(3)(a). The late payment fee is (subject to statutory caps) the greater of: (i) fifty percent of the amount of the deficient fees; or (ii) an amount equal to the transmittal fee; but the late payment fee shall not exceed an amount equal to fifty percent of the international filing fee not taking into account any fee for each sheet in excess of thirty sheets (see § 1.431(c)(1)-(c)(3) and (d)).
